subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sensitive-data sanitizer, keep this policy plugin-owned through reply/message hooks, or document the current SecretRef/log/tool-redaction limits without a new core sanitizer?
rationale: The request changes user-visible output and overlaps security defaults, SecretRefs, tool output, transcript redaction, plugin hooks, and channel delivery, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary or defaults.

options.title: Design a core sanitizer boundary
options.body: Define a narrow, security-reviewed core sanitizer using existing redaction helpers for approved final-reply and selected tool-output sinks, with explicit defaults and tests.

options.title: Keep sanitizer policy plugin-owned
options.body: Use reply_payload_sending/message hooks for an official or community sanitizer package and add only missing extension seams if current hooks are insufficient.

options.title: Document current limits
options.body: Decline automatic final-output filtering for now and document reliance on SecretRefs, log/transcript/tool redaction, filesystem isolation, and plugins.

recommendation.title: Design a core sanitizer boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow, security-reviewed core sanitizer using existing redaction helpers for approved final-reply and selected tool-output sinks, with explicit defaults and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This team owns the adjacent secrets/security surfaces and is the best available owner for the sensitive-data boundary decision.
